Watching families, children, and elderly people enjoy themselves together gave me a sense of community spirit and tradition . It was not just an ordinary fair; it was an experiencethat engaged all my senses, from the vivid sights and smells to the sounds of celebration. Even though it was noisy and crowded , I thoroughly enjoyed it, and it remains one of the most memorable experiences of my life. Follow-up Questions for Band 7.5+: 1. How do people usually behave in crowded places in Bangladesh? 2. What are the positive and negative aspects of visiting crowded events? 3. Do you think crowded places are more enjoyable than quiet places? Why? 4. How can overcrowding at festivals or fairs be managed effectively? 5. Do you prefer local fairs or modern entertainment venues? Why? 143. Describe a challenge you faced that you thought was rather difficult - You should say: - What it was - When and where you faced it - Why you thought it was a difficult challenge - And explain how you felt at the time One challenge that I faced, which I initially thought was extremely difficult, was learning the Spanish language. This happened about five years ago, shortly after I moved to Spain, where I needed to communicate effectively in both my daily life and professional settings. At first, I found the challenge daunting because Spanish is very different from my native language. The grammar rules, verb conjugations, and pronunciation were particularly tricky for me. For example, there were many tenses and subtle differences between formal and informal speech, which made it confusing. I also struggled to understand native speakers , especially in fast conversations or regional accents, which often left me feeling overwhelmed. I thought it was a difficult challenge because learning a language as an adult requires a lot of focus, patience, and consistent practice . I had to balance it alongside my work and other responsibilities, which made it even more demanding. I enrolled in a language course, watched online tutorials, and practiced with locals, which gradually improved my skills. At the time, I felt stressed and frustrated because progress was slow, and sometimes I worried that I might never master it. However, after consistent effort, I began to notice real improvement, and this gave me a great sense of achievement and confidence. Looking back, overcoming this challenge not only helped me adapt better to life in Spain but also taught me the importance of perseverance and determination when facing any difficult task. Follow-up Questions 1. Why do you think learning a new language can be challenging for adults? 2. How did learning Spanish help you in your personal or professional life? 3. Did you use any apps or online resources to help you learn Spanish? 4. How long did it take before you felt comfortable speaking Spanish?5. Do you plan to learn any other languages in the future? 144. Describe an ideal and perfect place where you would like to stay (e.g. a house, an apartment) - You should say: - Where it would be - What it would look like - What special features it would have - Whether it would be big or small

And explain why it would be an ideal place for you My ideal and perfect place to stay would be a peaceful duplex house, located in a quiet, green area away from the noise of the city. It would be practical, comfortable, and close to nature, making it easy to live a healthy and balanced life. The house would have a front garden where I could grow vegetables, fruits, and flowers, and a small pond nearby for fish. There would also be an open field or lawn where I could relax, do some exercise, or spend quality time with family. Inside, the house would combine functionality with tradition. I would have wooden or bamboo furniture, a well-organized kitchen, and simple but elegant decor. The staircase would be sturdy and made of wood, giving a natural feel. There would also be a comfortable living room where family and friends could gather, as well as a quiet reading corner or small library. For leisure, the house would have a balcony or rooftop sitting area, where I could enjoy fresh air and sunlight. The bedrooms would be designed to be comfortable and relaxing, providing privacy and peace. Overall, this ideal place would be spacious enough for a family but not unnecessarily large, blending comfort, simplicity, and practicality. I think it would be an ideal place because it allows me to live peacefully, stay close to nature, and maintain a balanced, happy life without unnecessary distractions. It feels like a place where one can focus, relax, and enjoy the little things in life. Follow-up Questions 1. Would you prefer living in a house or an apartment? 2. How important is it to live near nature? 3. Would you like to live alone or with family in your ideal home? 4. What features do you think every ideal home should have? 5. Do you think your ideal home would be in the city or countryside? 145. Describe an old friend you had lost touch with and got in contact with again - You should say:- Who he/she is - How you knew each other - Why you lost contact - How you got in contact again - And explain how you felt after getting in contact again One of the friends I lost contact with after school was my close friend Ilora. After finishing school in 1997, everyone became busy with their own lives and we gradually stopped communicating. Recently, something surprising happened. Ilora’s daughter came to England for her university studies, and through one of our mutual friends she managed to find my contact and called me. I was really surprised and happy to hear her voice after so many years. What touched me most was knowing that her daughter had grown up and come to the UK for study. I even felt as if my own niece was coming here. Although we had not spoken for many years, our connection felt the same. We talked about our school memories and l aughed about many silly things that happened back then. Reconnecting with her was truly heartwarming and it reminded me that true friendship can survive even after a long time. Possible Part 3 Follow-up Questions 1. Why do people sometimes lose contact with their friends? 2. Do you think it is important to stay in touch with childhood friends? 3. How has technology helped people reconnect with old friends? 4. Is it easier to make friends when people are young or when they are older? 5. What qualities help maintain a long-lasting friendship? 146. Describe something you did in your study/work that has made you feel confident - You should say: - When and where it happened - What you did - Why it made you feel confident - And explain how you felt about it Model Answer Something I did in my studies that made me feel very confident was learning the Spanish language. This happened when I moved to Spain in 2008 to live and work there. At the beginning, I found Spanish very difficult because the vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar were completely new to me. To improve, I enrolled in a language school, bought books and CDs, and attended classes regularly. Initially, it was very challenging, and I often felt like giving up. But I stayeddetermined and kept practicing every day. Gradually, I became comfortable with the language and could understand conversations and speak more fluently . Eventually, I took a level-one Spanish exam and passed it with a good score, which was a huge confidence booster. This achievement made me feel proud and motivated , because I had overcome a difficult challenge through hard work and persistence. It also gave me the confidence to continue learning until I reached C1 level , and it showed me that I can succeed if I stay focused and committed. Overall, it was a very rewarding experience that strengthened my self -belief and sense of accomplishment. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. How can learning a new skill increase someone’s confidence? 2. Do you think studying abroad helps improve self-confidence? Why? 3. Is it more important to succeed quickly or to keep trying despite difficulties? Why? 4. How can teachers or managers help students or employees feel more confident? 5. Are people more confident when they learn a language or a technical skill? Why? 147. Describe a picture/photograph of you that you like You should say: - Where it was taken/drawn - When it was taken/drawn - Who took/drew it - And explain how you felt about it Among all the pictures I have, there is one that is very special to me because it contains my family members, especially my four brothers. This photograph is very precious to me as it captures a beautiful moment of our family together. Interestingly, we actually have several similar pictures taken at different times in our lives. When I look at them, it feels really amusing because I can easily notice how our appearances have hanged over the years. For example, in the older photos we look much younger and more carefree, c whereas in the recent ones we look more mature and responsible. What makes this picture even more meaningful is the emotional connection it brings. At present, all of my brothers do not live together in the same house anymore because everyone is busy with their own lives and responsibilities. Therefore, whenever I see this photograph, it gives me a strong feeling of belonging and reminds me of the wonderful time we spent together. To be honest, looking at this picture always makes me feel quite nostalgic. It reminds me of our childhood memories, the fun we had together, and the strong bond we share as brothers. That is why this picture is one of my most beloved possessions. 148. Describe something that you did with someone/a group of peopleYou should say: - What it was - Who you did it with - How long it took you to do this - And explain why you did it together One memorable activity I did with a group of people was organising a charity bazaar in my community. The main aim of this event was to raise funds for people who were in need. Before the event, we had several meetings to plan everything properly. During these meetings, we divided the responsibilities among our team members. For example, some people were responsible for preparing homemade food, while others arranged handicrafts a nd decorative items to sell. A few members, including me, worked on organising the venue, setting the prices of the products, and promoting the event in the neighbourhood. In addition, we had to hire a suitable place for the bazaar and confirm the booking in advance. We also discussed how we would display the products and how the selling process would work. It required a lot of coordination and careful planning. On the day of the event, everyone worked enthusiastically. Many people from the community came to support us, and thankfully most of the items were sold. In the end, we successfully raised a good amount of money for charity. Although organising the event involved a great deal of hard work and sometimes it was quite stressful, it was an extremely rewarding experience. It taught us the real value of teamwork, cooperation, and dedication. Moreover, the sense of achievement we felt after successfully raising funds was truly unforgettable 149. Describe someone (a famous person) that is a role model for young people You should say: - Who he/she is - How you knew him/her - What he/she has done - And explain why he/she can be a role model for young people A famous person who is a role model for young people in my country is Dr. Muhammad Yunus. I first learned about him during my school days, when we studied notable personalities from Bangladesh who have made an impact globally. Later, I also read articles and watched interviews about his work. Dr. Yunus is known as the “father of microfinance” and the founder of Grameen Bank. He has dedicated his life to helping poor people, especially women, by giving them small loans to start businesses and improve their lives. Through this work, he has lifted millions of people out ofpoverty and empowered them to become self-reliant. He even received the Nobel Peace Prize for his remarkable contributions to social and economic development. I think he is an excellent role model for young people because he demonstrates compassion, determination, and social responsibility. He shows that one person can bring positive change in the world, and that education, creativity, and courage can help solve real problems. His life teaches young people to think beyond personal success and contribute to society in meaningful ways. Personally, I feel inspired by Dr. Yunus because he shows that helping others and being innovative can create a lasting impact. He encourages young people to be socially aware, responsible, and ambitious in a way that benefits the community as well as themselves. Follow-up Questions 1. Do you think young people in your country know enough about Dr. Yunus? 2. What qualities make someone a good role model? 3. Can social media influencers also be role models for young people? 4. How important is it for students to have role models? 5. Would you like to meet Dr. Yunus in person one day? 50. Describe a time when missed or were late for an important meeting/event You should say: - When it happened - What happened - Why you missed/were late for it - And explain how you felt about this experience One time I missed an important appointment was recently, on the 3rd of March. It was a medical appointment for my third dose of the Hepatitis B vaccine at my local GP clinic. This appointment was particularly important because it was the final dose, and completing the full course is necessary for proper protection. Unfortunately, the appointment was early in the morning, and the night before I woke up around 5:00 AM for Sahoor during Ramadan. After eating, I went back to sleep. Normally, I would set an alarm to wake up again, but that day I forgot. As a result, I overslept and completely missed the appointment. When I realized what had happened, I felt very guilty and embarrassed , because I knew the appointment was important and I should have been more careful. It was also quite frustrating since rescheduling the vaccine is not easy, and I might have to wait until next month for another slot. However, this experience taught me a valuable lesson about time management. Now, I always set multiple reminders or alarms in advance to make sure I don’t miss any important appointments again. 5 Follow-up Questions1. How do you usually manage your time for important appointments? 2. Have you ever been late for any other type of event or meeting? 3. Do you think people in general are careful about being on time? 4. How can technology, like alarms or calendar apps, help prevent missed appointments? 5. What do you do if you realize you are going to be late for something important?

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a live performance you enjoyed watching.
cue_card_points: Who performed in it- What kind of performance it was - When you watched it - And explain why you enjoyed One live performance that I will never forget was a Disney parade at Disneyland Park. It was a colourful and energetic parade featuring many famous cartoon characters. What made the experience truly special was that every character appeared in the exact same costumes and with the same music that I used to watch on television during my childhood. When Mickey Mouse and Minnie Mouse arrived with their classic theme song, I suddenly felt extremely nostalgic. To be honest, at that moment I completely forgot my age and almost turned into a child again. I was clapping, waving, and enjoying the performance with so much excitement. It brought back so many happy memories from my childhood when I used to watch those cartoons regularly. Interestingly, my children were quite shocked to see my reaction. They were laughing because I was behaving just like them—full of excitement and joy. For them, it was probably surprising to see their parent acting like a little kid. Overall, it was a magical experience that I will always remember because it connected my childhood memories with a real-life moment shared with my own children. 1. Why do people enjoy watching live performances instead of recorded shows? 2. Do you think live performances are more memorable than watching shows on TV? Why? 3. How do childhood characters like Mickey Mouse influence children’s imagination? 4. Why do adults sometimes feel nostalgic when they see things from their childhood? 5. Do you think events in places like Disneyland Park are important for family entertainment? Why? 56.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a person who helps to protect the environment.
cue_card_points: Who this person is - When this person does this - What has the person done - And explain why you think this is important One person I truly admire is Iqbal Habib, a well-known urban activist in Dhaka, Bangladesh. He has made a remarkable effort to keep the city clean and environmentally healthy. He works actively to improve urban environments by encouraging people to keep their surroundings tidy and free from waste. One of his major concerns is preventing mosquito breeding areas, especially stagnant water and dirty drains. As we know, mosquitoes can spread dangerous diseases such as Dengue Fever, so his work helps protect public health. What I find particularly impressive is that he does not only talk about problems but also takespractical action. He regularly organizes awareness campaigns and encourages communities to clean their neighbourhoods. Through these activities, he motivates ordinary citizens to take responsibility for their environment. In my opinion, his efforts benefit the community in many ways. Cleaner surroundings mean fresher air to breathe and fewer health risks for people. It also creates a more pleasant and liveable city for residents. Overall, I believe people like him play a vital role in protecting the environment and improving the quality of life in busy cities like Dhaka. 1. Why is it important for citizens to keep their cities clean? 2. What environmental problems do large cities like Dhaka face today? 3. Do you think governments or individuals should take more responsibility for environmental protection? Why? 4. How can communities prevent diseases like Dengue Fever that spread because of poor sanitation? 5. What can schools do to teach children about environmental responsibility? 6. Do you think public awareness campaigns are effective in changing people’s behaviour? 7. How can modern cities improve air quality and create a healthier environment? 57.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a sport that you really like.
cue_card_points: What it is - How often you do it - How you learned to do it - And explain why you like it One sport that I really like is the Marathon. It is a long-distance running race of about kilometres, and it requires a lot of endurance, patience, and determination. What I find most inspiring about this sport is the mindset of the runners. They have to train for months and push themselves through extreme fatigue to reach the finish line. One famous example is the London Marathon, which takes place every year in London and attracts runners from all over the world. Personally, I like this sport not only for its physical challenge but also for the philosophy behind it. I believe life is very similar to a marathon. In my view, people who manage their energy wisely and keep moving forward eventually succeed, just like marathon runners who reach the finish line. So, in a way, I see marathon running as a powerful metaphor for life. 1. Why do many people enjoy watching sports events? 2. Do you think marathon running is popular in your country?3. part2.cue_card_title: Describe a TV series you like.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a plan that you had to change recently.
cue_card_points: When this happened - What made you change the plan - What the new plan was - And how you felt about the changeModel Answer A plan that I had to change recently was my original idea of staying in Spain forever, but about five years ago, I ended up moving to the UK instead. At that time, I had been living in Spain for several years and was quite comfortable there. However, due to Brexit and its implications, especially for work and residence permits, I had to reconsider my plans. Additionally, I wanted to provide better educational opportunities for my children, which influenced my decision to move. As a result, I made a new plan to relocate to the UK. This opened up a lot of opportunities for me, both professionally and personally. I was able to explore multiple options for work and study, and my children also gained access to a different and high-standard education system. Initially, I felt a bit anxious and uncertain about leaving Spain, because I had grown attached to the place. But over time, I realized that the change was very positive. The move allowed my family and me to grow, adapt, and take advantage of new opportunities that we wouldn’t have had otherwise. In the end, I felt grateful and confident that this change, though unexpected, turned out to be the right decision. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. Why do people sometimes have to change their plans unexpectedly? 2. How do you usually react when your plans are disrupted? 3. Can changing plans be a positive thing? Why? 4. How do people make decisions when facing major life changes? 5. Do you think planning for the future is always necessary? 6. How has technology affected the way people plan their lives? 60.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a water sport you would like to try in the future.
cue_card_points: What it is - Where you would like to try it - Whether it is difficult - And explain why you would like to try it Model Answer A water sport that I would really like to try in the future is water sliding. I would like to try it at a famous water park, perhaps in Dubai or Thailand, where they have very large and exciting slides. From what I’ve seen in videos, some of these slides are very tall and steep, and the speed can be quite fast, so it might be a little challenging and scary at first. I want to try this sport because it looks extremely fun and exciting, and I enjoy doing activities that give a rush of adrenaline. It also seems like a great way to relax and enjoy water,especially during the summer. I imagine that the experience of sliding down, feeling the wind and water splash around me, would be both thrilling and refreshing. Overall, I think it would be a memorable and enjoyable activity, and I look forward to trying it whenever I get the chance. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. Why do people enjoy water sports? 2. part2.cue_card_title: Describe a time you enjoyed a free day off work or school.
cue_card_points: Where you were - What you did - Who you were with - And how you felt about it Model Answer A time I really enjoyed a free day off was during my college life, when I got a day off to attend my cousin’s wedding. We spent the whole day helping with preparations, decorating the venue, and participating in the wedding ceremonies. I also got to meet relatives and friends whom I hadn’t seen for a long time, which made the day even more enjoyable. I felt very happy and relaxed, because it was a break from the usual college routine. The atmosphere was festive and lively, with music, food, and laughter all around. I enjoyed every moment of it, from the ceremonies to the small moments spent chatting and taking photos with family. Overall, it was a memorable day, not just because of the wedding, but also because I got to spend quality time with my loved ones and truly enjoy a day off. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. Why do people enjoy having a day off work or school? 2. How do you usually spend your free time? 3. Is it important to have breaks from work or study? Why? 4. part2.cue_card_title: Describe a noisy place you have been to.
cue_card_points: Where it is When you went there What you did there And explain why you feel it’s a noisy place Model Answer A noisy place that I remember visiting was a village fair in my hometown back in 1995. Village fairs are quite common in rural areas of Bangladesh, and they usually attract a large number of people from nearby villages. I went there with my family and some relatives. The fair was extremely lively and crowded. There were many stalls selling traditional snacks, sweets, fruits, and local handmade toys. One toy that I clearly remember was called “tomtom,” which was very popular among children at that time. Many kids were buying and playing with those toys. The whole place was full of different sounds. There were vendors loudly calling customers, children screaming and laughing with joy, and music playing from loudspeakers. Because of the large crowd and all the activities happening at once, the atmosphere was very noisy and chaotic. Sometimes it was even difficult to hear the person standing next to me. Even though the noise was a bit irritating at times, I still enjoyed the experience because the fair was colorful, energetic, and full of cultural charm. It was a memorable moment from my childhood, and it gave me a chance to enjoy the festive environment and spend time with my family. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. Why do some people enjoy noisy places? 2. What are the disadvantages of living in a noisy environment? 3. How can noise pollution affect people’s health? 4. Do you think cities are becoming noisier nowadays? Why? 5. What measures can governments take to reduce noise pollution? 6. Do you prefer quiet places or lively places? Why? 63.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a disagreement you had with someone.
cue_card_points: Who you had the disagreement with What the disagreement was What happened And explain how you felt about it Model AnswerA disagreement I had was with a close friend over who should pay the bill at a restaurant. It happened a few months ago when we went out for dinner together. We both ordered food and drinks, and when the bill arrived, we realized we hadn’t agreed beforehand on how to split it. I thought it would be fair if we split the bill equally, but my friend insisted on paying for verything, saying it was his treat. I felt a little uncomfortable because I didn’t want to impose e or seem rude, but at the same time, I wanted to contribute my share. The discussion became a bit tense, as neither of us wanted to back down immediately. Eventually, we laughed it off and decided to share the payment, half and half, which resolved the disagreement. I felt relieved and satisfied because we found a solution without hurting our friendship. This situation reminded me that clear communication and compromise are important in avoiding misunderstandings. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. Why do disagreements happen between friends? 2. How can disagreements be resolved peacefully? 3. Is it better to avoid disagreements or confront them? Why? 4. How do disagreements affect relationships? 5. Do you think disagreements are sometimes useful? How? 6. How do cultural differences influence disagreements? 64.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a person you disliked at first but ended up being friends with.
cue_card_points: Who he/she is How you knew him/her Why you dislike him/her at first but changed your mind And explain how you feel about the experience Model Answer A person I disliked at first but ended up becoming good friends with is my school friend, Sajia Borna. I first met her in grade V at school. At the beginning, I didn’t feel very comfortable around her because she was so confident, hardworking, and always at the top of the class, while I was an average student and felt a bit insecure about my own abilities. Initially, I thought she might be too serious and strict, and I wasn’t sure we would get along. But as time passed, our teacher sat me next to her during class , and we started working together, especially during dictation and class exercises . I noticed how patient she was in helping me improve, and she also shared her study tips and knowledge generously. Gradually, I realized she was friendly, supportive, and very kind-hearted. Over time, we became very close friends, and I learned a lot from her, not only academically but also about discipline and dedication . Looking back, I feel really grateful for that experience because it taught me not to judge people too quickly and how friendships can develop inunexpected ways. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. Why do people sometimes dislike someone at first? 2. Can first impressions be misleading? How? 3. How important is it to give people a second chance? 4. Do friendships that start later in life differ from childhood friendships? 5. How do shared activities help people become friends? 6. Have you ever helped someone improve in school or work, like Sajia helped you? 65.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe an important thing you learned (not at school or college).
cue_card_points: What it wasWhen you learned it How you learned it And explain why it was important One area of science that I am very interested in and would like to read more about is immunotherapy. This is a field of medicine that focuses on using the body’s immune system to fight diseases, and it has a lot of exciting potential. I find it particularly fascinating because immunotherapy is not only being applied to cancer, but researchers are also exploring its use for conditions like arthritis and some skin diseases that are otherwise very difficult to cure. The idea that the body’s own defenses can be trained to fight serious illnesses is both innovative and inspiring. I would like to read more about this area because it combines biology, medicine, and technology in a way that can significantly improve human health. Understanding how immunotherapy works and what new treatments are being developed could be extremely useful in the future. Overall, I think immunotherapy is an exciting and promising field of science that has the potential to save many lives and improve the quality of life for people with chronic diseases. Possible Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. Why do you think people are interested in new medical discoveries? 2. How important is scientific research for improving human health? 3. Do you think governments should invest more in medical research? Why? 4. How can science help prevent diseases in the future? 5. Are there any risks in applying new medical technologies too quickly? 67.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a foreign country you would like to visit in the future.
cue_card_points: What it is - What you have known about it - Who you would like to go there with - And explain why you would like to visit it One foreign country that I would really like to visit is Egypt. It is famous for its rich history, both in terms of ancient civilization and religious heritage. The main reason I want to go there is to see the Pyramids of Giza, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. I have always been amazed by how people thousands of years ago were able to design and build such enormous structures without the modern tools we have today. Standing in front of the pyramids would allow me to appreciate the architectural knowledge and skills of that era. Besides the pyramids, I would also like to explore the Nile River, which is not only the longest river in Africa but also an essential part of Egyptian history and daily life. A boat ride along theNile would be a wonderful way to see the country and its beautiful landscapes. I am also very curious to visit the Mount Sinai, a place of great religious significance, and enjoy its natural scenery. part2.cue_card_title: Describe a line (or a few words) that you remember from a poem or song.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a time when you helped a child.
cue_card_points: When it was - How you helped him/her- Why you helped him/her - And how you felt about it Model Answer A time when I helped a child was when I was a second-year medical college student. The family was going through a very difficult situation because they also had a very small baby at home, so the parents could not stay in the hospital all the time to look after their sick daughter. Seeing their problem, I decided to stay in the hospital and take care of the child as much as I could. I stayed there for about seven days, helping with basic care and making sure she was comfortable. It was very challenging for me, because it was the first time I had such a serious responsibility, and I hardly slept during those days. Physically and mentally, it was probably one of the hardest tasks I had ever done at that time. However, I wanted to help because I felt a strong sense of responsibility and empathy for the family. They were my teachers, and I respected them a lot. Fortunately, the child gradually recovered and became healthy again. What makes this experience even more special is that that little girl has now grown up and become a doctor in the UK. Her parents still remember my help and are very grateful to me, which makes me feel proud and deeply satisfied. Looking back, I feel happy and fulfilled, because I was able to support someone in a difficult moment. It also strengthened my confidence and compassion as a future healthcare professional. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. Why is it important to help children when they are in difficulty? 2. What are some ways adults can support children’s well-being? 3. part2.cue_card_title: Describe a job that is useful to the society.
cue_card_points: What job it is - How do you know about this job? - What types of people do this job - And explain why you think this job is useful to the society When we talk about roles that form the backbone of any community, doctors and teachers are undoubtedly the two most essential professions. Whether it is a routine check -up or a life -saving surgery, a doctor’s expert ise allows people to return to their families and their work. In places like London or Dhaka, we see how vital they are —working around the clock to manage public health and provide comfort during our most vulnerable moments. Without them, the productivity and well-being of society would simply collapse. On the other hand, teachers are the architects of the future. While a doctor saves a life, a teacher shows that person how to live it meaningfully. They provide the tools—literacy, critical thinking, and social skills —that allow children to grow into produ ctive adults. As someone who values studies and uses AI to learn more efficiently, I see teachers as the original "guides" who help usnavigate a world full of information. They don't just teach facts; they instill values and confidence in the next generation. Both of these jobs require a true sense of calling. A doctor’s success is seen in a healthy community, and a teacher’s success is seen in a society that is educated, innovative, and kind. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. Describe a place you have been to and would like to recommend others to live there (not your hometown) You should say: - Where is it? - What the place is like - When you visited there - Who you went there with - And explain why you would recommend this place to others If you are looking for places in London that offer a real sense of community and convenience, I would highly recommend considering Ilford and Whitechapel. Having spent time in both, I’ve seen how they each offer a very different but equally valuable lifest yle, especially for those who ppreciate cultural diversity and easy access to the heart of the city. a Whitechapel is perfect if you love being in the middle of the action. It is incredibly vibrant and famous for its rich history and the iconic Whitechapel Market. What makes it a great place to live is its proximity to the City of London—you can practically walk to the major financial districts or the creative hubs of Shoreditch. For a student or a professional, the energy here is unmatched. You have world-class art at the Whitechapel Gallery and some of the best authentic food in the city right on your doorstep. It’s a place that never sleeps and always feels alive. On the other hand, Ilford offers a slightly more relaxed, residential feel while still being very well- connected. It is a fantastic option for families because you get more space for your moneycompared to inner London. With the Elizabeth Line, you can get into Central London incredibly fast, giving you the best of both worlds. Ilford has great shopping at the Exchange mall and beautiful green spaces nearby like Valentines Park, which is perfect if you enjoy those morning walks I find so refreshing. I recommend these areas because they are melting pots of culture. You can find everything from traditional South Asian spices to modern cafes. Living in these spots allows you to experience the true, multicultural heart of London while staying connected to all the opportunities the city provides. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. Describe a time that something changed your life in good ways You should say: - When and where it happened - What happened - How you felt about it - And explain how it changed your life in good ways Having children is, without a doubt, the most profound and life -changing experience I have ever gone through. It is the moment when your center of gravity shifts entirely; suddenly, you are no longer the protagonist of your own story—they are. Before I became a parent, my life was focused on my own goals, my studies, and my personal time, but now, every decision I make is filtered through the lens of what is best for them. The most immediate change was the sense of responsibility . It can be overwhelming at first to realize that another human being is completely dependent on you for everything. It forced me to become much more disciplined and patient than I ever thought possible. Those quiet morning walks in the fields or the hours spent studying at the library became much more precious because they are now the rare moments I have to recharge so I can be the best parent I can be. However, the most beautiful change is the unconditional love and the way children make you see the world with fresh eyes. Watching them discover something for the first time —whether it’s aladybug in the grass or a new book —brings back a sense of wonder that we often lose as adults. They have taught me more about r esilience and joy than any textbook ever could. While life is certainly much busier and more exhausting now, it is also infinitely more meaningful. My children are my greatest motivation to keep pushing forward with my studies and my writing, because I want to build a future that they can be proud of. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. Describe a countryside area that you have been to ou should say: Y - Where is it? - When and why you went there - Who you went there with - And explain how you felt about it If we focus specifically on the countryside of County Cork, it is a place that feels incredibly vast and rugged. While it’s right next to Kerry, Cork has a character all its own—often called the "Rebel County." The landscape there is a beautiful mix of rolling green hills, hidden valleys, and a dramatic coastline that feels like the edge of the world. One of the most memorable parts of the Cork countryside is the West Cork region. It is much quieter than the big cities, and the air smells like a mix of sea salt and fresh grass. I remember driving through small, colorful villages like Kinsale or Glengarriff, where the pace of life slows down completely. The fields are divided by old stone walls that have been there for centuries, and you’ll often see sheep or cattle grazing peacefully, completely unbothered by the rest of the world. A real highlight of the Cork countryside is the Blarney Castle grounds. Beyond the famous castle itself, there are sprawling gardens and forest walks that feel almost magical. Walking through the "Rock Close" feels like stepping into a fairy tale, with ancient trees and hidden pathways. For someone like me who loves a quiet walk in a field every morning, the countryside in Cork is like a much larger, wilder version of that peace. It’s a place where you can truly get lost in nature and forget about the stress of studies or city life. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. Did I visit any of the coastal cliffs in Cork, or did I spend most of my time exploring theinland greenery and forests? 2. Describe an invention that is useful in your daily life You should say: - What is the invention? - What it can do How popular is it? - Whether it is difficult or easy to use - And explain why it is useful When it comes to inventions that truly change the quality of daily life, I think the vacuum cleaner is right at the top of the list. Describe a time when someone askedfor your opinion You should say: - Who asked for your opinion - Why he/she wanted to know your opinion - What opinion you gave - And explain how you felt when he/she asked for your opinion In our culture, a marriage program is much more than just a single day; it is a series of elaborate events that bring two families together. Describe a time you used your cellphone/smartphone to do something important You should say: - What happened - When it happened- How important the cellphone/smartphone was - And explain how you felt about the experience In 2026, the way we use our smartphones for class has completely changed because of how convenient they have become as all-in-one study hubs. It is no longer just about checking an email or a quick schedule; my phone is now the primary way I manage my enti re academic life on the go. Whether I am commuting, waiting between appointments, or just have a few quiet minutes at home, I can access my entire digital classroom right from my pocket. If I am struggling to understand a complex theory from a lecture, I can simply open an AI assistant on my phone and ask for a simplified explanation or a real-world example. I also use it to scan my handwritten notes or printed handouts, which the phone then converts into digital, searchable text that I can organize into study guides. This level of convenience means that I never feel like I am falling behind, even on my busiest days, because my study materials are always with me and easier than ever to navigate. Later, I also read articles and watched interviews about his work. Dr. Yunus is known as the “father of microfinance” and the founder of Grameen Bank. He has dedicated his life to helping poor people, especially women, by giving them small loans to start businesses and improve their lives. Through this work, he has lifted millions of people out ofpoverty and empowered them to become self-reliant. He even received the Nobel Peace Prize for his remarkable contributions to social and economic development. I think he is an excellent role model for young people because he demonstrates compassion, determination, and social responsibility. He shows that one person can bring positive change in the world, and that education, creativity, and courage can help solve real problems. His life teaches young people to think beyond personal success and contribute to society in meaningful ways. Personally, I feel inspired by Dr. Yunus because he shows that helping others and being innovative can create a lasting impact. He encourages young people to be socially aware, responsible, and ambitious in a way that benefits the community as well as themselves. Follow-up Questions 1. Do you think young people in your country know enough about Dr. Yunus? 2. What qualities make someone a good role model? 3. Can social media influencers also be role models for young people? 4. How important is it for students to have role models? 5. Would you like to meet Dr. Yunus in person one day? 50. Describe a time when missed or were late for an important meeting/event You should say: - When it happened - What happened - Why you missed/were late for it - And explain how you felt about this experience One time I missed an important appointment was recently, on the 3rd of March. It was a medical appointment for my third dose of the Hepatitis B vaccine at my local GP clinic. This appointment was particularly important because it was the final dose, and completing the full course is necessary for proper protection. Unfortunately, the appointment was early in the morning, and the night before I woke up around 5:00 AM for Sahoor during Ramadan. After eating, I went back to sleep. Normally, I would set an alarm to wake up again, but that day I forgot. As a result, I overslept and completely missed the appointment. When I realized what had happened, I felt very guilty and embarrassed , because I knew the appointment was important and I should have been more careful. It was also quite frustrating since rescheduling the vaccine is not easy, and I might have to wait until next month for another slot. However, this experience taught me a valuable lesson about time management. Now, I always set multiple reminders or alarms in advance to make sure I don’t miss any important appointments again. 5 Follow-up Questions1. How do you usually manage your time for important appointments? 2. Have you ever been late for any other type of event or meeting? 3. Do you think people in general are careful about being on time? 4. How can technology, like alarms or calendar apps, help prevent missed appointments? 5. What do you do if you realize you are going to be late for something important?

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a time that something changed your life in good ways.
cue_card_points: When and where it happened - What happened - How you felt about it - And explain how it changed your life in good ways Having children is, without a doubt, the most profound and life -changing experience I have ever gone through. It is the moment when your center of gravity shifts entirely; suddenly, you are no longer the protagonist of your own story—they are. Before I became a parent, my life was focused on my own goals, my studies, and my personal time, but now, every decision I make is filtered through the lens of what is best for them. The most immediate change was the sense of responsibility . It can be overwhelming at first to realize that another human being is completely dependent on you for everything. It forced me to become much more disciplined and patient than I ever thought possible. Those quiet morning walks in the fields or the hours spent studying at the library became much more precious because they are now the rare moments I have to recharge so I can be the best parent I can be. However, the most beautiful change is the unconditional love and the way children make you see the world with fresh eyes. Watching them discover something for the first time —whether it’s aladybug in the grass or a new book —brings back a sense of wonder that we often lose as adults. They have taught me more about r esilience and joy than any textbook ever could. While life is certainly much busier and more exhausting now, it is also infinitely more meaningful. My children are my greatest motivation to keep pushing forward with my studies and my writing, because I want to build a future that they can be proud of. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. How did the birth of my first child specifically change my daily routine and the way I manage my study time? 2. What is one lesson my children have taught me about patience that I didn't know before? 3. Do I find that being a parent has made me more creative or focused when I sit down to do my writing? 4. How do I balance the "me time" I need (like my morning walks) with the constant demands of looking after a family? 5. Has having children changed the long-term career goals I have for myself? 80. Describe a countryside area that you have been to ou should say: Y - Where is it? - When and why you went there - Who you went there with - And explain how you felt about it If we focus specifically on the countryside of County Cork, it is a place that feels incredibly vast and rugged. While it’s right next to Kerry, Cork has a character all its own—often called the "Rebel County." The landscape there is a beautiful mix of rolling green hills, hidden valleys, and a dramatic coastline that feels like the edge of the world. One of the most memorable parts of the Cork countryside is the West Cork region. It is much quieter than the big cities, and the air smells like a mix of sea salt and fresh grass. I remember driving through small, colorful villages like Kinsale or Glengarriff, where the pace of life slows down completely. The fields are divided by old stone walls that have been there for centuries, and you’ll often see sheep or cattle grazing peacefully, completely unbothered by the rest of the world. A real highlight of the Cork countryside is the Blarney Castle grounds. Beyond the famous castle itself, there are sprawling gardens and forest walks that feel almost magical. Walking through the "Rock Close" feels like stepping into a fairy tale, with ancient trees and hidden pathways. For someone like me who loves a quiet walk in a field every morning, the countryside in Cork is like a much larger, wilder version of that peace. It’s a place where you can truly get lost in nature and forget about the stress of studies or city life. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. Did I visit any of the coastal cliffs in Cork, or did I spend most of my time exploring theinland greenery and forests? 2. How did the "quiet" of the Irish countryside in Cork compare to the atmosphere of the fields I walk in back home? 3. Did I get a chance to visit a local farmhouse or try some of the famous artisan cheeses that West Cork is known for? 4. What was the most surprising thing about the weather in Cork—did the "four seasons in one day" happen during my visit? 5. Did the rugged beauty of the Cork landscape inspire me to write anything new or take up a bit of travel photography? 81.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe an invention that is useful in your daily life.
cue_card_points: What is the invention? - What it can do How popular is it? - Whether it is difficult or easy to use - And explain why it is useful When it comes to inventions that truly change the quality of daily life, I think the vacuum cleaner is right at the top of the list. Living a busy life with studies and a family means that keeping a home clean can often feel like a never-ending battle. Before I really started using a high-quality vacuum, I used to spend so much time and physical energy sweeping, and even then, it never felt perfectly dust-free. The reason this invention is so useful to me is the sheer efficiency and convenience it offers. It can pick up fine dust, pet hair, and small debris from carpets and hard floors in a fraction of the time it takes to do it manually. In a city like Dhaka, where dust seems to find its way into every corner of the house, having a powerful vac uum is a total lifesaver. It doesn't just make the floors look better; it actually makes the air in the rooms feel fresher and healthier for my children. What I find most impressive about modern vacuums —especially the newer cordless or robotic versions—is how they’ve turned a tiring chore into something almost effortless. I can quickly clean up a mess in the kitchen or give the living room a refresh without breaking a sweat. It’s a perfect example of how a bit of engineering can give us back our most valuable resource: time. Instead of spending an hour cleaning, I can get it done in ten minutes and get back to my writing or my books. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. Do I prefer using a traditional upright vacuum with a cord, or have I switched to a more modern, lightweight cordless model? 2. How often do I find myself using the vacuum during the week—is it a daily quick-fix or part of a big weekend deep clean? 3. Have I ever considered getting a robot vacuum that can clean the floors automatically whileI’m busy with my studies? 4. Does anyone else in my family, like my brother or the kids, help out with the vacuuming, or is it a task I prefer to handle myself? 5. What is the most satisfying part of vacuuming for me—seeing the clean carpet lines or earing the sound of the dust being sucked up h 82.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a difficult decision that you made and had a good result.
cue_card_points: What the decision was - When you made that decision - Why it was difficult to make - And explain how you felt about the good result Model Answer A difficult decision that I made but which had a very good result was deciding to learn the Spanish language. I made this decision when I was living in Spain several years ago. At that time, I realized that without learning Spanish it would be difficult for me to communicate with local people and manage daily activities. The decision was quite difficult because learning a new language as an adult is not easy. I was already busy with work and other responsibilities, so I had to invest a lot of time and effort. At the beginning, I also felt nervous because I was not confiden t about speaking in a completely new language. However, after thinking about the long -term benefits, I decided to enroll in a Spanish language course and practice regularly. I tried to speak with local people, watch Spanish television programs, and read simple texts to improve my vocabulary and pronunciation. Fortunately, the results were very positive. Over time, I became much more comfortable communicating in Spanish, which made my life in Spain easier and more enjoyable. I could interact with people more naturally and understand the culture better. When I finally realized that I could speak Spanish confidently, I felt extremely proud and satisfied. It gave me a strong sense of achievement and also boosted my confidence to learn other languages and explore new cultures. Looking back, even though it wa s a difficult decision at first, it turned out to be one of the best decisions I have ever made. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. Why are some decisions difficult to make? 2. Do people usually make important decisions alone or with advice from others? 3. How can difficult decisions help people grow in life? 4. Do young people and older people make decisions differently? 5. What can people do if they realize they made the wrong decision?83.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a time when someone askedfor your opinion.
cue_card_points: Who asked for your opinion - Why he/she wanted to know your opinion - What opinion you gave - And explain how you felt when he/she asked for your opinion In our culture, a marriage program is much more than just a single day; it is a series of elaborate events that bring two families together. Recently, a close relative of mine asked for my opinion on how to plan their Gaye Holud (the turmeric ceremony) and the main wedding reception. Since I have always been interested in organizing events and have a good sense of current trends, they wanted to know my thoughts on balancing our deep-rooted traditions with a few modern touches. I suggested that for the Gaye Holud, they should keep the traditional elements like the vibrant yellow themes and the classic ritual of applying turmeric paste, but perhaps add a bit of a modern twist with the music and the stage decor. They also asked for my advice on the menu for the reception, specifically whether to stick to the classic Kacchi Biryani or introduce some different appetizers. I shared my opinion that while people always look forward to the traditional flavors, having a few unique starters would make the event stand out. It felt really good to be consulted on such an important family occasion. It wasn't just about the logistics; they valued my perspective on how to make the guests feel welcome while ensuring the bride and groom remained the center of attention. Sharing my opinion helped them feel more confident in their decisions, and it made me feel like an active part of the family’s joy. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. Was I nervous about giving my opinion on such an important family event, or did I feel confident because I know their tastes so well? 2. Did they end up following all of my suggestions, or did they decide to go with a more traditional route for the marriage program? 3. If I were the one planning the whole wedding from scratch, what is the first thing I would prioritize to make it a success? . How do I personally feel about the modern "Bollywood-style" dance performances that are becoming popular in Bangladeshi weddings nowadays? 5. If someone asked for my opinion on the guest list, would I suggest a large, grand celebration or a smaller, more intimate gathering of close family? 84.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a time you used your cellphone/smartphone to do something important.
cue_card_points: What happened - When it happened- How important the cellphone/smartphone was - And explain how you felt about the experience In 2026, the way we use our smartphones for class has completely changed because of how convenient they have become as all-in-one study hubs. It is no longer just about checking an email or a quick schedule; my phone is now the primary way I manage my enti re academic life on the go. Whether I am commuting, waiting between appointments, or just have a few quiet minutes at home, I can access my entire digital classroom right from my pocket. The real game-changer is how AI is integrated into almost every app I use. If I am struggling to understand a complex theory from a lecture, I can simply open an AI assistant on my phone and ask for a simplified explanation or a real-world example. I also use it to scan my handwritten notes or printed handouts, which the phone then converts into digital, searchable text that I can organize into study guides. This level of convenience means that I never feel like I am falling behind, even on my busiest days, because my study materials are always with me and easier than ever to navigate. Beyond just finding information, my phone helps me stay disciplined. I use AI-powered scheduling apps that automatically adjust my study sessions based on my progress and upcoming deadlines. It even helps me refine my writing by suggesting better sentence structures or checking my tone while I am drafting an essay. This seamless blend of technology and education has turned my smartphone into a powerful tool that saves me hours of manual work, allowing me to focus on actually learning and enjoying my subjects. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. Which specific AI-powered app has become my absolute favorite for organizing my daily class schedule and notes? 2. Do I find that I prefer using voice commands to ask my phone questions during a study session, or do I still like typing things out? 3. How has the convenience of having my studies on my phone affected my ability to take breaks and disconnect from school work? 4. Have I tried using any of the new AI tools that can turn my lecture notes into instant practice quizzes or flashcards? 5. Since my phone is now such a vital part of my education, what steps do I take to make sure it stays a tool for productivity rather than a distraction? 85.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a way/change that helps you save a lot of time.
cue_card_points: What is it? - How do you implement it? - How difficult is it?- And explain how you feel about the way/change In my busy life, where I am constantly trying to balance my studies and my family, the biggest change that has helped me save a lot of time is using AI. Before I started using these tools, I used to spend hours searching through websites or thick textbooks just to find one specific answer or to understand a difficult concept. Now, I can get the information I need in a matter of seconds. What I love most about AI is how it can take something very complicated and explain it to me in a simple way. If I’m stuck on a difficult chapter in my studies, I can ask the AI to summarize the main points or give me a clear example, which saves me from f eeling frustrated and stuck for hours. It’s like having a personal tutor available at any time of the day or night, which is a huge help when I’m trying to fit my learning into small gaps in my schedule. It also helps me with organizing my thoughts. Sometimes, I know what I want to say, but I’m not sure how to start or how to structure my writing. The AI helps me create an outline or suggests a better way to phrase a sentence, so I can finish my work much faster than I could on my own. This technology has truly changed my daily routine, giving me back precious time that I can then spend with my children or simply taking a much-needed break. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. What was the first thing I used AI for that made me realize just how much time it could save e? m 2. Do I feel that using AI makes me more creative, or does it just help me get the boring tasks done faster? 3. How do I make sure that I am still learning and thinking for myself while using these tools for my studies? 4. Is there a specific part of my day, like the morning or late at night, when I find AI to be the most helpful? 5. Have I shared any of these AI tools with my friends or family members to help them save time as well? 86.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a friend you like to talk with.
cue_card_points: Who is he/she - What do you like to talk about - Why do you like to talk with him/her - And explain how you feel about him/her Model Answer A friend I really like to talk with is my friend Shuly. She is very close to me, and in many ways, I feel she is more like a sister than just a friend. We have known each other for quite a long time, and over the years we have built a strong and supportive friendship. Shuly works at a GP surgery, where she helps patients and supports the local community through her work in healthcare. Because of her job, she is a very patient, caring, and responsible person. I truly admire the way she manages her professional responsibilities while still being kind and supportive to people around her. When we talk, we usually discuss many different topics, such as our daily lives, work experiences, personal challenges, and future plans. Sometimes we also talk about family matters, studies, and ways to stay motivated in life. Our conversations are always meaningful and encouraging. The reason I enjoy talking with her is that she has a very positive and optimistic attitude. Whenever I feel stressed or overwhelmed, especially with studies or responsibilities, she always encourages me and gives thoughtful advice. Her words often make me feel calmer and more confident. Overall, I feel very grateful to have a friend like her in my life. She is supportive, inspiring, and compassionate. Talking with her always lifts my mood and reminds me that good friendships can make life much easier and more meaningful. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. Why is it important to have friends to talk with? 2. What topics do friends usually discuss with each other? 3. Do people today communicate with friends more online or face to face? 4. How can good friends influence a person’s life? 5. Is it better to have many friends or a few close friends? Why? 87.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a time when you were stuck in a traffic jam.
cue_card_points: When it happened - Where you were stuck - What did you do while waiting - And explain how you felt in the traffic jam Being stuck in a traffic jam when you have a deadline is incredibly stressful, and I remember one specific occasion when I was heading to the train station. I had a very important journey to make, and I had timed everything perfectly, but I didn't account for the unpredictable nature of the road that day. As I was sitting in the back of the car, I realized the traffic had come to a complete standstill. All I could see in front of me was a sea of red brake lights and rows of buses and cars that weren't moving an inch. I kept checking my watch every few minut es, and the closer it got to the train's departure time, the more my heart started to sink. The noise of the honking horns and the heat of the day made the waiting feel even longer. I felt so helpless because there was absolutely nothing I could do to make the cars move faster. Itried to stay calm, but I was constantly calculating how many minutes I had left before the gates at the station would close. It was a huge test of my patience. In the end, it taught me that no matter how well you plan your schedule, you always need to leave a massive "buffer" of extra time, especially when you are traveling to somewhere as time-sensitive as a train station. Follow-Up Questions 5 1. Did I eventually make it to the station on time to catch the train, or did I have to wait for the next one? 2. What was the reason for the traffic jam —was it an accident, roadwork, or just the usual rush hour? 3. How did I try to pass the time while I was sitting in the car waiting for the traffic to move? 4. Did I try to take a different route or get out and walk, or was I completely trapped in the middle of the road? 5. How did this experience change the way I plan my trips to the station or the airport now? 88. Describe a quiet place you like to go - Where is it? - How you knew it - How often do you go there? - What do you do there? - And explain how you feel about the place When I need to escape the noise of my daily life and really focus on my studies, my favorite place to go is the library. In a world that is always so loud and fast -paced, the library feels like a completely different universe where silence is respected and everyone is there for the same purpose of learning. I love the specific atmosphere of a library—the smell of the books, the soft sound of pages turning, and the way everyone moves quietly so as not to disturb others. It is the only place where I feel I can truly leave my worries at the door and dive deep in to my books. Because it is so calm, my mind stops racing, and I find that I can get more work done in two hours there than I can in a whole day at home. Finding a small corner table near a window is my favorite way to spend an afternoon. Even when the library is full of people, it still feels private and peaceful. This quiet environment is essential for me, especially when I have a lot of difficult material to cover for my studies. It’s more than just a place to read; it’s a space where I feel productive, motivated, and completely at peace. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. Do I have a specific library that I always visit, or do I like to explore different ones in the city? 2. What is my favorite section of the library to sit in—do I prefer being surrounded by old books or in a more modern study area? 3. How do I feel when I leave the quiet of the library and have to step back into the noisy streets?4. Do I find that I study better when there is absolute silence, or do I like a little bit of background hum from other people? 5. Is there a particular time of day when the library feels the most peaceful and inspiring to me? 89.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe something that surprised you and made you happy.
cue_card_points: What it was - Who did this? - How you found out about it and what you did - And explain why it surprised you and made you happy I have always liked nature, but I was recently very surprised by how much joy and peace keeping plants could bring into my life. I never really thought of myself as someone with a "green thumb," but I decided to get a few indoor plants just to brighten up the house. To my surprise, watching them grow and thrive has become one of the things that makes me the happiest. What surprised me the most was how rewarding it feels to see a new leaf unfurl or a flower finally bloom after weeks of waiting. It’s a very slow process, but there is something so satisfying about knowing that my care and attention helped that plant survi ve. In my busy life, where everything feels so fast and sometimes stressful, the quiet and steady growth of my plants reminds me to slow down and be patient. It also surprised me how much the greenery changed the atmosphere of my home. The rooms feel much more alive and fresher now. Every time I walk past them and see how healthy they look, it gives me a little boost of happiness. It’s a small hobby, but it has had a big impact on my mood and has taught me that even the simplest things in nature can bring a lot of comfort and surprise. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. What was the very first plant I bought that started this whole passion for gardening? 2. Do I prefer easy-to-care-for plants like succulents, or do I enjoy the challenge of looking after more delicate flowers? 3. How do I feel when one of my plants isn't doing well —do I get stressed, or do I enjoy the rocess of trying to "save" it? p 4. Have I started sharing my passion by giving small plants or cuttings as gifts to my friends and family? 5. Does the time I spend watering and caring for my plants feel like a form of meditation for me during the day? 90.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a family member who you want to work with in the future.
cue_card_points: Who is he/she - Whether you worked together before- What kind of work would you like to do with him/her - Explain how you feel about this family member I have always thought it would be amazing to work with my brother in the future. We have a very strong bond, and because we grew up together, we already understand how each other thinks and works. Even though we are different individuals, our skills actual ly complement each other quite well, which I think is the most important part of a successful partnership. The reason I want to work with him is that I know I can trust him completely. In any professional environment, trust is hard to find, but with my brother, I wouldn't have to worry about hidden agendas. He is someone who is very driven and hardworking, and his energy always motivates me to do my best. Whether it’s starting a small business together or collaborating on a creative project, I feel like we would be a great team because we can be honest with each other without any hesitation. I also think we would have a lot of fun while working. Even when things get stressful, we have the same sense of humor, so we could probably find a way to laugh through the challenges. Having a partner who understands your background and shares your values would make the journey toward our goals so much more meaningful. To me, building something successful with a family member like him would be the ultimate achievement. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. What kind of business or specific project do I imagine us starting together in the future? 2. Since we are siblings, how would we handle it if we had a serious disagreement about a work- related decision? 3. Do we have similar professional backgrounds, or would he handle the technical side while I focus on the creative side? 4. Does he know that I have this goal of working with him, and is he just as excited about the idea as I am? 5. What is one quality my brother has that I think would make him a great boss or business partner? 91. Describe a job that one of your grandparents did
What was the job about
Was this only the one job she or he did

How you felt about it One of my grandparents had a very distinguished career as a Joint Secretary in the government. It was a position of great responsibility and respect, and I always felt a sense of pride hearing about the work they did. Being a Joint Secretary meant they wer e a high -ranking official involved in making important decisions and helping to run a whole department or ministry. The job was quite demanding because it required a lot of discipline and a deep understanding ofhow the country works. They had to attend many high -level meetings, manage a large team of staff, and draft important policies that affected many people's lives. I remember hearing about the long hours they spent at the office and the many files they had to review carefully. It wasn't just about giving orders; it was about being a leader and a problem-solver for the public good. Even though I didn't see the day -to-day work myself, I could see the qualities it built in them — they were incredibly organized, calm under pressure, and very articulate. Seeing the way people looked up to them made me realize how much hard work and dedication it takes to reach that level in a professional career. It has definitely inspired my own passion for my studies and my desire to achieve something meaningful in my life. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. Which specific government department or ministry did my grandparent work for during their time as Joint Secretary? 2. Did they ever share stories with me about a particularly difficult decision or a big project they handled at the office? 3. How did they manage to balance such a high -pressure, important job with their family life at home? . Do I feel that I have inherited any of the leadership qualities or the disciplined habits that my grandparent developed through their career? 5. What was the most valuable piece of professional advice they ever gave me based on their years of experience in the civil service? 92.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe something you do to keep fit and healthy.
cue_card_points: What is it? - When you do it - Who do you do it with - Why is it important to keep fit and healthy - Explain why it can help you keep fit and healthy For me, staying fit and healthy isn't about going to a crowded gym or doing anything too intense; it’s really about the simple habit of taking a walk in a field every morning. Since my life is usually so full of responsibilities with my studies and my fami ly, having that quiet time outdoors is the best way for me to start my day. I love the feeling of the fresh air and the open space of the field before the rest of the world really wakes up. It’s a very peaceful experience where I can just clear my head and breathe deeply. Even though it's just a walk, it helps me feel physically e nergized and mentally prepared for whatever the day is going to bring. I don't usually set a timer or a specific distance; I just walk at a steady pace and enjoy the naturearound me. It’s the one time in the day when I don't have to think about my books or my household chores. This simple routine has become essential for me because it keeps my body moving and gives me a sense of calm that lasts until I get back home to my busy life. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. Do I prefer to take these morning walks completely alone to enjoy the silence, or do I sometimes listen to music or a podcast? 2. How long do I usually spend walking in the field before I have to head back and start my daily routine? 3. Does the changing weather or the seasons affect how much I enjoy my morning walk, or do I go out even when it's a bit cold or rainy? 4. Have I noticed a big difference in my energy levels or my mood on the days when I miss my morning walk? 5. Is there a specific spot in the field, like a certain tree or a view, that I always look forward to reaching during my walk? 93.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe an occasion that you lost something in public.
cue_card_points: What you lost - When and where you lost it - What did you do to find it - Explain how you felt about it Losing something as important as a passport is always stressful, but losing it in a place as crowded and fast-paced as the streets of Dhaka is on a whole different level. It was definitely one of the most frantic experiences I’ve ever had. I remember I was out in a very busy area, probably navigating through the endless rows of rickshaws and people, when I realized my bag felt a bit too light. I stopped in the middle of the pavement and searched through every single pocket, but my passport was nowhere to be found. In a city like Dhaka, where thousands of people are moving past you every minute, the chances of finding something so small and valuable felt almost zero. My heart was racing because I kept thinking about all the trouble it would be to replace it, especially with my studies and everything else going on. I retraced my steps as best as I could, pushing through the crowds and asking shopkeepers if they had seen anything. The noise of the honking horns and the heat of the city made it even harder to stay calm. It was such a helpless feeling, standing there in the middle of the bustling street, realizing that something so essential was just gone. It really taught me a lesson about being extra careful with my belongings whenever I'm in a crowded public space. 5 Follow-Up Questions1. Did I eventually manage to find the passport, or did I have to go through the long process of applying for a new one at the passport office? 2. Who was the first person I called for help or advice when I realized the passport was missing in such a crowded place? 3. How did the experience change the way I carry my important documents now when I’m traveling or out in public? 4. Were the people around me in the street helpful when I was frantically searching and asking if anyone had seen it? 5. How long did it take for me to stop feeling anxious every time I checked my bag after that day? 94.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a special day out that cost you little money/didn't cost you much.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe something youdo that can help you concentrate on work/study.
cue_card_points: What is it? - How it helps you concentrate - When you do it - And explain how you feel about it Model Answer One thing that really helps me concentrate on my work or study is meditation along with the Pomodoro method . These two techniques help me stay focused and manage my time more effectively. Meditation is something I usually do for a few minutes before I start studying or working. I sit quietly, close my eyes, and focus on my breathing. This simple practice helps me calm my mind and reduce stress. When my mind is relaxed, it becomes much easier for me to concentrate on the task in front of me. The second technique I use is the Pomodoro method, which is a time -management strategy. In this method, I work for about minutes with full concentration, and then I take a short break of around five minutes . After repeating this cycle several times, I take a longer break. This approach helps me avoid mental fatigue and keeps my energy level steady throughout my study session. I usually follow these techniques when I have to study for exams or complete important tasks that require deep concentration. They help me stay disciplined and prevent distractions such as checking my phone or losing focus. Overall, I feel very satisfied and productive when I use these methods. They make my study sessions more organized and efficient, and I can complete my work with better quality. Because of this, meditation and the Pomodoro technique have become an important part of my daily routine. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1.
