Is it better to study for a long time continuously or take breaks? Why? 97.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a traditional product in your country.
cue_card_points: What is it? - When you tried this product for the first time- What it is made of - Explain how you feel about it If you ask anyone about a traditional product from Bangladesh, the first thing that comes to mind is the Jamdani sharee. It isn't just a piece of clothing for us; it is a piece of our history and a form of art that has been passed down through generations. What makes Jamdani so special is that it is entirely handmade. The weavers don’t use machines or even draw the patterns on the fabric beforehand. Instead, they weave those beautiful floral and geometric designs directly into the fine muslin cloth while it is still on the loom, which is just incredible to think about. Because the fabric is so thin and high -quality, it feels as light as air. This makes it perfect for the hot weather we have in Bangladesh, but it still looks incredibly elegant and expensive for any big event. For us, wearing a Jamdani—especially on special occasions like Eid or weddings—is a way of showing our true heritage. Even UNESCO recognized it as a masterpiece of human heritage. Even though we have so much modern fashion now, nothing really compares to the grace of a real, hand-woven Jamdani. It’s a treasure that almost every Bangladeshi woman dreams of having in her collection. 5 Follow-Up Questions 1. Do I have a favorite Jamdani sharee that was passed down to me by my mother or grandmother for a special occasion? 2. When I am choosing a Jamdani for an event like Eid, do I usually go for the classic white and old or do I like more vibrant, modern colors? g 3. How can we better support the local weavers in villages like Sonargaon so this beautiful art doesn't disappear in the future? 4. Since a real Jamdani takes months to make and can be quite an investment, do I think it is better to own one high-quality piece or several cheaper, machine-made ones? 5. How does it make me feel when I see people from other countries admiring or wearing our traditional Jamdani art? 98.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe an invention that has changed the world in a positive way.

Students can learn from online courses, educational websites, and digital libraries without leaving their homes. Another important benefit is that the internet helps people in their professional lives and businesses. Many companies now operate online, and people can work remotely or run businesses through digital platforms. It has also created many new career opportunities in areas such as information technology, digital marketing, and online services. The internet influences people of all age groups. For young people, it is a powerful learning tool and a way to stay connected with friends. Adults often use it for work, banking, shopping, and staying updated with news. Even older people benefit from it because they can communicate with family members through video calls or social media. Overall, the internet has completely changed people's lifestyles . It has made the world more connected and has made information easily accessible to everyone. Because of these reasons, I believe the internet is truly a revolutionary invention that has improved people's lives in many ways. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. part2.cue_card_title: Describe a time you were very busy.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a popular/well-known person in your country.
cue_card_points: Who is this person? - What he/she has done - Why he/she is popular - And explain how you feel about this person Model Answer A popular and well-known person in my country is Dr. Muhammad Yunus, who is often called the “Banker to the Poor.” He is a Nobel Laureate and the founder of the Grameen Bank, which provides microloans to people in Bangladesh who do not have access to traditional banking. His work has helped millions of poor people, especially women, to start small businesses and improve their lives. Dr. Yunus is also known as the chief advisor of the interim government of Bangladesh at one point, and he proposed the “Three Zero” idea, which aims for a world with zero poverty, zero unemployment, and zero net carbon emissions. He has delivered speeches at many international events and his books are taught in universities around the world . People respect him for his leadership, hard work, and dedication , and he is considered an icon and role model in Bangladesh. I really admire Dr. Yunus because he is a compact package of inspiration, intelligence, and humanity. cue_card_points: What is the song? - What story the song tells - Whether the song is popular - And explain why you think it is interesting Model Answer An interesting song that I really like is “Shopno Jabe Bari Amar” by Grameenphone, which I first heard on TV and social media. The song highlights their struggles, sacrifices, and longing to return home , especially during festivals like Eid when everyone misses their loved ones. The song is quite popular in Bangladesh because it connects deeply with people who can relate to the feelings of separation and the importance of family. It is accompanied by a heart -touching video showing workers calling their families and sharing small moments of happiness despite the distance. I find this song interesting and inspiring because it is more than just music —it conveys a powerful message about love, family, and human emotions. Listening to it makes me reflective,emotional, and grateful for the relationships I have in my life. It’s a song that stays with you long after you hear it. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. Do you think listening to songs can influence people’s emotions? How? 2. Are songs important in festivals or special occasions in your country? 3. How have people’s tastes in music changed over the years? 4. Do you prefer modern songs or traditional songs? Why? 5. Can music help people feel connected to their culture? How? 115.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe an interesting discussion you had with your friend.
cue_card_points: What the discussion was about - What opinions you and your friend had - Why do you think the discussion was interesting? - And how you felt about it Model Answer An interesting discussion I had with my friend was about the impact of social media on young people. We were sitting at a café last month and started talking about how platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok influence behavior, learning, and social interactions. I shared my opinion that social media can be distracting and sometimes harmful because it encourages comparison and reduces face -to-face communication. My friend, on the other hand, believed that it is useful for learning, staying connected, and even building a career if used wisely. We discussed both the advantages and disadvantages , giving examples from our own experiences and from news we had seen. I found the discussion very interesting because we both had strong, differing viewpoints, yet we listened to each other carefully. It made me think more deeply about my own habits and the ways social media affects people around me. After the discussion, I felt stimulated and reflective, and I appreciated how a simple conversation with a friend could open my mind to new perspectives. It reminded me that good discussions are not just about agreeing, but about learning from each other. Follow-up Questions (Part 3) 1. Do you think discussions with friends help improve your thinking skills? 2. How important is it to respect other people’s opinions during a discussion? . Can online discussions be as effective as face-to-face discussions? Why or why not? 3 4. Do you think discussions at school or college help students understand topics better? 5. How can disagreements in a discussion be handled politely? 116. Describe a thing you did to learn another languageYoushould say: - What language have you learned? - What did you do? - How it helped you learn the language - And how you felt about it Model Answer A thing I did to learn another language was learning Spanish when I moved to Spain in 2008. At first, I found the language extremely challenging because the grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation were very different from what I knew. To improve, I enrolled in a Spanish language course and bought books, CDs, and online courses. I practiced every day, repeating phrases aloud, listening to audio lessons, and trying to communicate with local people whenever I could. I also watched Spanish TV shows and read simple articles to improve my understanding. This approach really helped me because I combined formal learning with practical usage. Over time, I became more confident in speaking and understanding Spanish. It also made daily life in Spain much easier and more enjoyable. I felt very proud and accomplished as I gradually improved. Learning a new language taught me patience, persistence, and gave me a sense of achievement. It was challenging, but also incredibly rewarding because it opened new opportunities for communication, work, and cultural understanding. Follow-up Questions 1. Do you think learning a foreign language is easier when you live in that country? 2. What is the best way to learn a language quickly? 3. Is it more important to focus on speaking or writing when learning a language? 4. How do you stay motivated when learning a difficult language? 5. Can learning a new language help you understand other cultures better? 117.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a rule you dislike and would like to change in the future.
cue_card_points: What is it? - What is it for? - Why don't you like it - And explain why you would like to change it odel Answer (Regenerated) M One rule that I really dislike and would like to change in the future is the law that ordinary citizens are not allowed to catch or physically stop a thief when they see someone stealing. I understand that this rule exists to prevent violence and protect people from harm, but I feel it can be unfair in some situations. For example, if someone sees a thief stealing their property or someone else’s in front of them, they might want to act immediately. However, the law generally states that only the police are authorized to handle criminals, which sometimes allows thieves to escape before any action can be taken. I would like to change this rule to create a system where people can safely intervene without breaking the law. For instance, there could be guidelines that allow citizens to hold a thief in a non-violent way until the police arrive . This change could help reduce crime , make neighborhoods safer, and give ordinary people a sense of responsibility and protection. Overall, I think this rule could be improved to balance safety with justice , so people can act responsibly without fear of legal consequences. Follow-up Questions1. Do you think people should have the right to defend their property? 2. What are the risks if citizens try to catch thieves? 3. How can the police improve crime prevention? 4. Are there countries where citizens are allowed to stop thieves legally? 5. How can communities help reduce theft without breaking the law? 119.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe an item of clothing that someone gave you.
cue_card_points: What the clothing was - Who gave it to you - When you got it - And explain why this person gave you the clothes Model Answer (Regenerated) An item of clothing that someone gave me is a dokhmanda, which is a traditional Bangladeshi shawl. The shawl is made of soft, warm fabric and has beautiful colors with delicate embroidery , which makes it both practical and elegant. People usually wear a dokhmanda in winter to keep warm, but it is also considered suitable for special occasions because of its traditional and stylish look. I really like this item because it is comfortable, versatile, and culturally meaningful. This gift is particularly special to me because it came from my mother. Every time I wear it, I feel her love and care, and it also reminds me of my Bangladeshi heritage. It’s not just a piece of clothing; it’s a symbol of family connection and cultural pride, which makes it very dear to me. Follow-up Questions 1. Do you often receive clothes as gifts? 2. How important are gifts of clothing in your culture? 3. Do you prefer traditional or modern clothes as gifts? 4. Have you ever given clothing as a gift to someone? 5. How do you decide what type of clothing to wear for a special occasion? 120.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a city that you think is very interesting/famous.
cue_card_points: Where is it? - What it is famous for - How you knew this city - And explain why you think it is very interesting/famous Model Answer A city that I think is very interesting and famous is Anaheim in California, USA, which is hometo Disneyland. part2.cue_card_title: Describe a time you visited a new place.
cue_card_points: Where the new place is - When you went there - Why did you go there? - And explain how you feel about the place One new place I visited, which I found extremely exciting, was Disneyland. part2.cue_card_title: Describe a story someone told you and you remember.
cue_card_points: What the story was about - Who told you this story - Why do you remember it? - And how do you feel about it One story that someone told me and I still remember vividly is the story of the Talking Tortoise. I first heard this story from my mother when I was a child. It is a well-known folktale in Bangladesh that carries an important moral lesson about the dangers of talking too much. In the story, there was a tortoise who loved to talk constantly. One day, two boys were planning to attack him, and an eagle came to help. The eagle told the tortoise to hold on with his mouth, and he would carry him safely to the sky . However, while flying, the tortoise could not resist speaking and opened his mouth. As a result, he fell from the sky, and his shell cracked. I remember this story so clearly because it is both entertaining and educational. It taught me that sometimes, saying too much can get you into trouble , and it reminded me of the value of thinking before speaking. Even now, whenever I feel tempted to gossip or speak hastily, I recall this story, and it helps me control my words. I feel grateful to my mother for sharing such stories because they are both fun and full of life lessons. Follow-up Questions: 1. Do you like listening to stories from your parents? 2. What kind of stories do you enjoy the most? 3. Do you think children learn more from stories than from textbooks? 4. Have you ever told this story to someone else? 5. Why do you think folktales are popular in Bangladesh? 123.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe an important river/lake in your country.
cue_card_points: Where is it located - How big/long it is - What it looks like - And explain why it is important Here’s a Band 7-style IELTS cue card response for your topic, with keywords highlighted and follow-up questions: An important river in Bangladesh that I would like to talk about is the Jamuna River. It is one of the largest rivers in the country and serves as a major waterway for transportation and trade. The Jamuna is actually a channel of the Brahmaputra River, and it flows through several regions before joining the Padma River. The river is very wide and long, with fertile banks that are ideal for farming. Many people rely on it for fishing, agriculture, and daily transportation. The Bangabandhu Bridge, one of the largest bridges in Bangladesh, spans the Jamuna and connects the eastern and western parts of the country, which is very important for commerce and travel. During the rainy season , the river sometimes causes floods and erosion , which affects local communities. Despite this, the Jamuna River is extremely important for the economy, environment, and daily life of millions of people. It is not only a natural resource but also a vital part of the cultural and social life of Bangladesh. ollow-up Questions: F 1. Are there any other important rivers in Bangladesh? 2. How do people use rivers in your country for daily life? 3. Do rivers in Bangladesh face environmental problems? 4. Have you ever visited the Jamuna River? How was it? 5. Why do you think rivers are important for a country’s economy? 126.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe an old person you know who has had an interesting life.
cue_card_points: Who is this person? - Where he/she lives - What he/she has done in his/her life - And explain how you feel about him/her One old person I know who has had an interesting and remarkable life is my grandfather, Mr. M. Hafizuddin Khan. He lives in Bangladesh and has had a long and distinguished career in public service. He was born in 1939 and completed his B.A (Hons) and M.A in Political Science. He started his career in 1965 by joining the Pakistan Railway Accounts Service and gradually held several important positions in government audit. In 1977, he became a Deputy Secretary, a role he served in for about six years. Later, he worked as Director of Finance at BRDB, then as Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Works, the Internal Resources Division, and the Ministry of Local Government. Over the years, he was also a Member-Director of Finance at BADC and served as Additional Secretary in the Prime Minister’s Office. In 1994, he was promoted to Secretary and served in the Ministry of Disaster Management & Relief and the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications. Finally, on 8th August 1996, he became the Comptroller & Auditor General of Bangladesh , one of the highest positions in the country. Beyond his professional achievements, he received extensive training at home and abroad in public administration and participated in numerous seminars and workshops in countries such as the Philippines, Malaysia, Kenya, Nepal, Indonesia, Thailand, Geneva, Iran, Pakistan, USA, India, Canada, and the UK. I feel very proud and inspired by my grandfather because his life shows dedication, hard work, and leadership. He has achieved so much while maintaining humility and integrity, and he is a true role model for our family and for young people in Bangladesh. 5 Follow-up Questions 1. What qualities do you admire most in your grandfather? 2. Do you think young people today can learn from the experiences of older generations? 3. How important is international exposure and training for a successful career? 4. What challenges do you think he might have faced during his long career? 5. How does your grandfather inspire other members of your family? 127.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe a positive change that you have made recently in your daily r outine.
cue_card_points: What the change is - How you have changed the routine - Why you think it is a positive change - And explain how you feel about the change Recently, I made a positive change in my daily routine by adjusting my sleep schedule to go to bed earlier. To achieve this, I started a digital detox at least an hour before sleep, avoiding phones, computers, and TVs because the blue light from screens can disrupt melatonin production and make it harder to fall asleep. I also set a consistent wake-up time every morning, which helps regulate my circadian rhythm and makes it easier to feel naturally drowsy at night. Additionally, I transformed my bedroom environment into a calm and relaxing space by reducing light and removing distractions. These changes have led to better sleep quality, more energy during the day , and improved focus and productivity . Overall, I feel refreshed, motivated, and proud of this change because it has had a noticeable impact on both my physical health and mental well-being. Follow-up Questions: 1. Why do you think some people have trouble maintaining a healthy sleep routine? 2. How does a good sleep schedule affect your productivity during the day? 3. Do you think technology affects sleep habits? How? 4. Have you ever tried other methods to improve your sleep? What worked? 5. part2.cue_card_title: Describe a time when you answered a phone call from someone you didn’t know in a public place –.

part2.cue_card_title: Describe your favourite food at a traditional festival or a special event in your country -.
cue_card_points: What it is - At which festival/event you eat it - How it is made - And explain why you like it In my country, one of the most special foods people enjoy during festivals is biryani, especially during Eid al-Fitr or Eid al-Adha. It is my favourite festival food because it is rich, flavorful, and always shared with family and friends, creating a sense of togetherness. Biryani is a famous rice dish made with long-grain basmati rice, tender meat such as chicken, beef, or mutton, and aromatic spices like saffron, cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves. The rice and meat are slow-cooked together, which makes it very fragrant and tasty. Sometimes, people also add fried onions, boiled eggs, potatoes, or raisins on top for extra flavor. During Eid, families wake up early, wear new clothes, and visit relatives. A big pot of biryani iseither prepared at home or ordered from a restaurant, and everyone enjoys it together at lunch, often accompanied by salad, yogurt raita, or spicy curry. What makes biryani special for me is not only the taste but also the joyful atmosphere. Eating biryani during Eid reminds me of family gatherings, laughter, and celebration, which is why it is my favourite traditional festival food. Follow-up Questions: 1. Do you usually cook this food at home or buy it from a restaurant? 2. Are there any other traditional foods you enjoy during festivals? 3. How important is food in your country’s festivals? 4. Do you think traditional foods are losing popularity among young people? 5. Have you ever tried making biryani yourself? 134.
